analysis.investment_thesis: IXIGO is an interesting India-Bharat travel platform with strong revenue growth (68.5% 6Y CAGR) and finally turning FCF-positive (₹118 Cr in FY25), but at ₹7,837 Cr market cap and 133x P/E it fails every SMILE valuation test. The stock is fully discovered, institutionally crowded, and priced for perfection with ROE of only 9.74%.
key_strengths: Bharat-focused OTA with strong train/bus booking moat via ConfirmTkt + AbhiBus acquisitions, targeting underpenetrated Tier 2/3 India
Asset-light model with 81.74% gross margins and near-zero debt (D/E: 0.04), with FCF turning meaningfully positive at ₹118 Cr in FY25
Operating leverage visible: EBITDA grew from ₹36 Cr (FY23) to ₹83 Cr (FY25) as revenue scaled to ₹914 Cr
key_risks: Valuation is prohibitive — 133x trailing P/E and 57x forward P/E leaves zero margin of safety; any growth disappointment will crush the stock
FY25 net profit (₹60 Cr) actually DECLINED from FY24 (₹73 Cr) — FY24 was inflated by ₹39 Cr other income vs only ₹23 Cr in FY25, masking thin core profitability
Duopoly pressure from MakeMyTrip (backed by Ctrip) with far deeper pockets and brand dominance in the flight/hotel segments where margins are better
red_flags: Market cap ₹7,837 Cr — 8x outside SMILE sweet spot of <1,000 Cr; no information asymmetry possible
FII holding at 64.19% — this is an institutional darling, not an undiscovered gem; zero Kedia edge here
ROE of only 9.74% — well below my 15% threshold, unacceptable for a tech-first platform business at 133x earnings
Net profit regression in FY25 vs FY24 despite 39% revenue growth — operating margin at just 7.08% is dangerously thin for this multiple
analysis.detailed_analysis:
IXIGO's business story is genuinely interesting — it carved a niche in train and bus ticketing for Bharat travellers that MakeMyTrip ignored, and the ConfirmTkt/AbhiBus acquisitions create a multi-modal platform with strong brand recall in Tier 2/3 cities. Revenue scaling from ₹40 Cr (FY19) to ₹914 Cr (FY25) at 68.5% CAGR is a testament to the structural India travel megatrend. Operating cash flow has turned strongly positive at ₹122 Cr in FY25, and near-zero debt (D/E: 0.04) means the balance sheet is clean. These are the makings of a decent long-term compounder.

However, from a SMILE standpoint, this stock fails on almost every criterion I care about. At ₹7,837 Cr market cap and 133x P/E, there is no margin of safety — I would need this company to sustain 40-50% profit CAGR for 5+ years just to justify entry at today's price. With FIIs owning 64% of the float, the stock is already widely owned and analysed — any edge I might have from independent research is non-existent. The actual profitability quality is also worrying: FY25 PAT of ₹60 Cr fell below FY24's ₹73 Cr, largely because FY24 had ₹39 Cr in "other income" (likely IPO/investment gains) masking the weak core operating earnings. At 7.08% operating margin against an 81% gross margin, there is significant cost leakage that needs to be fixed before this is investable at any reasonable price. I'll watch from the sidelines and revisit if market cap corrects to sub-₹2,000 Cr or if operating margins cross 15%.
